Description: Simulated cognitive diagnosis data modeled on the Diagnosing Teachers' Multiplicative Reasoning (DTMR) assessment (990 respondents, 27 binary items, 4 attributes); not the real DTMR responses. Generated from the LCDM. True attribute profiles are in cov_true_*, true item parameters (intercept, main effects, one interaction) in itemcov_true_*, and the Q-matrix in qmatrix1-4.
Reference: Thompson W (2026). dcmdata: Data Sets for Diagnostic Classification Modeling. R package version 0.2.0. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=dcmdata. Simulated from parameters in Bradshaw, L., Izsák, A., Templin, J., & Jacobson, E. (2014). Diagnosing teachers' understandings of rational numbers: Building a multidimensional test within the diagnostic classification framework. Educational Measurement: Issues and Practice, 33(1), 2-14, and Izsák, A., Jacobson, E., & Bradshaw, L. (2019). Surveying middle-grades teachers' reasoning about fraction arithmetic in terms of measured quantities. Journal for Research in Mathematics Education, 50(2), 156-209.
Notes: dcmdata objects dtmr_data, dtmr_true_profiles, dtmr_true_items, dtmr_qmatrix. Q-matrix attribute order: 1 referent_units, 2 partitioning_iterating, 3 appropriateness, 4 multiplicative_comparison. itemcov_true_* NA = term not in that item's generating model (contributes 0). Class proportions (dtmr_true_structural) not included. Script data/simsyn/dtmr_sim.R.

Description: Simulated joint response accuracy and response time (van der Linden hierarchical framework): 1,000 persons x 20 items, normal-ogive accuracy and lognormal times; true ability and speed in cov_true_*, true item accuracy and time parameters in itemcov_true_*.
Reference: van der Linden, W. J. (2007). A hierarchical framework for modeling speed and accuracy on test items. Psychometrika, 72(3), 287-308. Generated with LNIRT::simLNIRT (Fox, J.-P., & Klotzke, K., LNIRT R package, version 0.5.1).
Notes: IRW's own seeded draw (seed 20261001, rho = 0.3). rt = exp(simulated log time). Script data/simsyn/lnirt_sim.R (#2725).

Description: Simulated two-class Rasch mixture (Rost 1990, design 2): 1,800 persons x 10 items, item difficulties reversed between classes; true class and ability in cov_true_*, class-specific difficulties in itemcov_true_*.
Reference: Rost, J. (1990). Rasch models in latent classes: An integration of two approaches to item analysis. Applied Psychological Measurement, 14(3), 271-282. Generated with psychomix::simRaschmix (Frick, Strobl, Leisch & Zeileis, 2012, Journal of Statistical Software 48(7)).
Notes: IRW's own seeded draw (seed 20261001), design 'rost2', extremes kept. Script data/simsyn/raschmix_rost2_sim.R (#2725).

Description: Simulated item preknowledge with response times: 1,000 persons x 40 items, 2PL scores and lognormal times; 10% of examinees know 40% of the items (scores redrawn at P = .90, log times x 0.75). True ability, speed and preknowledge flag in cov_true_*, true item parameters and compromised flag in itemcov_true_*.
Reference: Sinharay, S. (2017). Detection of item preknowledge using likelihood ratio test and score test. Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics, 42(1), 46-68. Generated with aberrance::sim (Gorney, K., & Deng, J., aberrance R package, version 0.3.0).
Notes: IRW's own seeded draw (seed 20261001); design of the aberrance detect_pk example with N = 1,000. rt in seconds. A response is contaminated when cov_true_preknowledge = 1 and itemcov_true_compromised = 1. Script data/simsyn/aberrance_pk_sim.R (#2725).

Description: Simulated test speededness with end-of-test rapid guessing: 1,000 persons x 40 items, 3PL scores and lognormal times; 10% of examinees guess (P = .25, 1-10 s) on the last 4 items after a change point. True ability, speed and speeded flag in cov_true_*, true item parameters and speeded-block flag in itemcov_true_*.
Reference: Shao, C., Li, J., & Cheng, Y. (2016). Detection of test speededness using change-point analysis. Psychometrika, 81(4), 1118-1141. Generated with aberrance::sim (Gorney, K., & Deng, J., aberrance R package, version 0.3.0).
Notes: IRW's own seeded draw (seed 20261001); design of the aberrance detect_cp example with N = 1,000. rt in seconds. A response is a rapid guess when cov_true_speeded = 1 and itemcov_true_speeded_block = 1. Script data/simsyn/aberrance_speeded_sim.R (#2725).

Description: Simulated longitudinal skill growth (higher-order hidden Markov cognitive diagnosis model): 1,000 persons x 50 DINA items over 5 waves (10 items per wave, counterbalanced blocks, 4 skills). True learning ability and per-wave skill mastery in cov_true_*, true slip/guess in itemcov_true_*, Q-matrix in qmatrix1-4.
Reference: Wang, S., Yang, Y., Culpepper, S. A., & Douglas, J. A. (2018). Tracking skill acquisition with cognitive diagnosis models: A higher-order, hidden Markov model with covariates. Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics, 43(1), 57-87. Generated with hmcdm::sim_alphas and sim_hmcdm (hmcdm R package, version 2.1.3).
Notes: IRW's own seeded draw (seed 20261001); HO_sep learning model with the package example's lambdas, Spatial Rotation Learning Program design (Q_matrix, Test_order). cov_true_alpha1-4 vary by wave. Script data/simsyn/hmcdm_learning_sim.R (#2725).

Description: Simulated binary symptom data from a known Ising network: 1,000 persons x 20 nodes, random graph (edge probability 0.2), squared-normal edge weights. True node thresholds, degrees and the full edge-weight matrix in itemcov_true_* (itemcov_true_w_itemKK = weight to itemKK).
Reference: van Borkulo, C. D., Borsboom, D., Epskamp, S., Blanken, T. F., Boschloo, L., Schoevers, R. A., & Waldorp, L. J. (2014). A new method for constructing networks from binary data. Scientific Reports, 4, 5918. Generated with IsingSampler::IsingSampler (Epskamp, S., IsingSampler R package, version 0.5.0).
Notes: IRW's own seeded draw (seed 20261001); one condition of van Borkulo et al. (2014). The paper's threshold rule is read as N(-s/2, (s/4)^2) truncated to [-s, 0], s = weighted degree (see script header). No person-level truth (none in the model). Script data/simsyn/ising_network_sim.R (#2725).

Description: Simulated rater effects under the hierarchical rater model: 1,000 persons x 6 items x 3 raters (fully crossed), scores 0-3; raters differ in bias and variability. True ability in cov_true_theta, item parameters and item-by-rater bias (phi) and variability (psi) in itemcov_true_*; rater column identifies the rater.
Reference: Patz, R. J., Junker, B. W., Johnson, M. S., & Mariano, L. T. (2002). The hierarchical rater model for rated test items and its application to large-scale educational assessment data. Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics, 27(4), 341-384. Generated with immer::immer_hrm_simulate (Robitzsch, A., & Steinfeld, J., immer R package, version 1.5.13).
Notes: IRW's own seeded draw (seed 20261001); design of the immer_hrm Example 1 with N = 1,000 and 6 items. Stage-1 ideal ratings are not returned by the generator and are not included. Script data/simsyn/hrm_rater_sim.R (#2725).
